Kelvaroq is a public Rust runtime built on VIctory and victory-fork. It adds rendering patches and measured submission improvements, and runs GTA VI through the prologue and first mission.
Public source under GPL-3.0, with pinned upstream revisions and a documented patch series
The prologue is playable at about 10 fps, with 7-8 fps in heavier views
An external 36-minute RTX 4090 playtest reached the first mission without a crash
CPU submission and synchronization remain the main bottleneck
Missing shader pipelines, 7% dropped draws and VRAM pressure remain
One-session stability evidence and two-platform performance measurements are limited
36-minute external playtest

An NVIDIA fork of VIctory on readmet3xt-lab's foxhound, with DLSS, frame generation and an in-game settings menu. PortWatch has verified it: about as playable as the leaders, at 20 fps without frame generation and without crashes.
Platform in its README: GeForce RTX 5070 12 GB, Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 64 GB RAM, Windows 11
20 fps without frame generation, no crashes, verified by PortWatch. README: 26-30 fps in the opening
DLSS upscaling and frame generation, 2x to 6x on RTX 50 cards, switched from an in-game F1 menu
No ray tracing by default; switching it on gives about 3 fps and a broken picture
Repository and GitHub account removed by GitHub on Nov 27 for a Terms of Service violation, confirmed by PortWatch. Its progress still counts in our overall number.
Belo Top Dawg

DexNom Runtime, a fork of VIctory for AMD Radeon, tested on a Radeon RX 7900 XTX. It builds on ZSlayerHQ's victory-world-runtime with its own fixes for shaders, texture streaming and GPU memory. PortWatch has seen it running with ray-traced lighting working, the first AMD build on our board to get it. Its picture is the best-rated on our board, though lighting and materials still have problems, and it plays through missions at about 3-4 fps (about 1 fps with ray tracing on), rarely crashing.
Ray-traced lighting working, seen by PortWatch: the first AMD build on our board to get it
Best-rated picture on our board; plays through missions
Translates 25,742 of the 25,758 shaders in its test archive; all 2,191 vertex shaders pass Microsoft's DXIL validator (its report)

AvatarManz's VIctory fork for the AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX, verified by PortWatch at about 16 fps on average, with sound. Its code and GitHub account were removed by GitHub on 27 Nov for a Terms of Service violation, as Belobug's were, which PortWatch has confirmed.
Platform: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX, Intel Core i9-12900K, 64 GB RAM, Windows 11
About 16 fps on average in game, verified by PortWatch. Its README: 13-20 fps indoors in the prologue, 19-22 on the first boat mission, 30 in menus

A private group's build on JoshuuDev's victory-amd fork of VIctory, verified by PortWatch. It runs GTA VI with ray-traced lighting at about 3-5 fps, almost never crashes, and the owner rates its story progress at 80%. The in-game phone renders really well, and the map menu runs at a higher frame rate. It's built mostly for AMD and also works on NVIDIA, at a lower frame rate. Code not public.

A build shown on darkworldhm's Rumble stream on 25 Nov, running GTA VI's free roam at about 12-15 fps, swinging between 5 and 24: the highest frame rate on our board. The owner rates its story progress at 80%, and it hasn't crashed so far. The picture looks alright, with some texture or ray-tracing glitches. Reportedly on an NVIDIA RTX 50-series card. It's built on VIctory, but which fork isn't known. Code not public.

Its GTA VI results (world at about 5 fps, cutscenes, a contributor's report of the first two missions) come from victory-fork's code, now copied into the repo, so they earn it no milestone.
